newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks climb to fresh record close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks climb to fresh record close.

text.p: French stocks rose to a fresh record close on Friday after a ground-breaking advance on Wall Street helped lift the bourse's leading index to an all-time high above 2,800 points.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 8.27 points, or 0.3 percent, at 2,784.28 after easing from its session and all-time high of 2,804.51 points.
The bourse will be closed on Monday for Pentecost.
The CAC-40 May futures contract rose 11 points to 2,780.
Volume was a heavy 9.37 billion francs.
The CAC index has risen 5.71 percent on the week after five sessions of gains despite some weakness in the dollar.

The market was bolstered by Wall Street's first ever close above 7,300 points on Thursday and recent opinion polls showing the conservative RPR-UDF coalition widening its lead over the Socialists in the upcoming May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.
Shares in Carrefour, a favourite of stock-pickers, chalked up the largest gain of the CAC 40. It rose 2.24 percent to 3,885 francs.

Schneider shares slumped 5.02 percent to 320 francs after the electrical equipment supplier reported first-quarter sales that disappointed the market. Brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu cuts its rating on the stock and other investment firms cut earnings estimates.
